title: Recognition of learner's personality traits through digital annotations in distance learning
reason: Digital annotation traces from an online reading environment (i-Read) used to score conscientiousness and neuroticism, compared with NEO-IPIP questionnaire scores (Pearson correlation, RMSE). Meets I4. Correlation coefficients themselves are not printed; only mean, RMSE, p.

extraction.design: validation study (system vs questionnaire), Pearson correlation and RMSE

extraction.population: academic volunteers aged 22–50, majority graduate students (some with professorship degree)
extraction.lms_indicators: digital annotation traces (highlighting, comments etc.) during reading sessions in i-Read

extraction.notes: No Pearson r is printed: verified against the PDF (p. 44, Tables 4-5), where the 'i-Read system' row contains only dots and the Neo-IPIP row gives Mean, RMSE, p-value. Fig. 11 scatterplot (neuroticism) shows wide dispersion. The 100 volunteers are the same people as the authors' earlier model-building study ('All the invited people have participated in our previous experimentation (Omheni et al., 2014)'), so validation is not on an independent sample. Population mixes graduate students with academics; E3 borderline. Only two of five traits evaluated.
